title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: A Police Salary Victoria Example
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using the 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, and a police salary Victoria example with Fair Work and ATO figures.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52. The average full-time weekly earnings in Victoria is $2,041.10, but this is an average, not a specific police salary Victoria figure.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading rate and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of leave entitlements. The Fair Work Ombudsman sets this loading. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. When using our timesheet, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading; do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary by your employer. It applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For example, on an annual gross of $80,000, super would be $80,000 × 0.12 = $9,600, added to your total remuneration. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost for the employer.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the first step is to convert it to an annual figure. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week for a full year, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For a typical full-time worker, the Fair Work Commission defines a standard week as 38 hours. So if you earn $30 per hour, your annual gross would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280.

It can also be helpful to think in fortnights. A fortnightly pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2. For the same $30 per hour, weekly pay is $30 × 38 = $1,140, so fortnightly pay is $2,280 before tax.

### Example Using Victoria’s Average Weekly Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings in Victoria averaged $2,041.10 per week. That is an average across all industries and occupations, not a median for any specific job. To find the implied hourly rate, divide by 38: $2,041.10 ÷ 38 ≈ $53.71 per hour. This average is useful as a benchmark, but it does not represent a **police salary Victoria** figure. Police pay in Victoria is determined by enterprise agreements and awards, which may differ from this average.

## Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

Australia has a National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave.

Many workers are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher minimum rates. For example, the Police (Victoria) Award or the Victoria Police Enterprise Agreement specifies pay rates for different ranks and classifications. If you are researching a **police salary Victoria**, you should check the relevant award or agreement rather than relying on averages.

When using our [timesheet](/), you enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual, tick the box to add 25% casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

For more on award rates, see our [pay guides](/blog). For detailed tables, visit our [reference tables](/data).

## Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Pay

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate your take-home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy.

### 2026–27 Tax Rates (Resident)

| Taxable income | Tax on this income |
|----------------|-------------------|
| $0 – $18,200 | Nil |
| $18,201 – $45,000 | 15¢ for each $1 over $18,200 |
| $45,001 – $135,000 | $4,020 plus 30¢ for each $1 over $45,000 |
| $135,001 – $190,000 | $31,020 plus 37¢ for each $1 over $135,000 |
| $190,001+ | $51,370 plus 45¢ for each $1 over $190,000 |

### Medicare Levy

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For 2026–27, the single reduction thresholds are based on 2025–26 figures (not confirmed for 2026–27 in this estimate). If your income is below a certain threshold, the levy may be reduced or waived. For most full-time workers, the full 2% applies.

### Example Tax Calculation

Take the Victoria average weekly earnings of $2,041.10. Annualised: $2,041.10 × 52 = $106,137.20. Using the tax brackets:
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201–$45,000: ($45,000 – $18,200) × 0.15 = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001–$106,137.20: ($106,137.20 – $45,000) × 0.30 = $18,341.16
- Total tax: $4,020 + $18,341.16 = $22,361.16
- Medicare levy: $106,137.20 × 0.02 = $2,122.74
- Total tax and Medicare: $24,483.90
- Estimated take-home pay: $106,137.20 – $24,483.90 = $81,653.30

This is an estimate only. It does not include HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more precise calculation, use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your gross pay. The super guarantee applies up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For the example above, super would be $106,137.20 × 0.12 = $12,736.46, bringing total remuneration to $118,873.66.

Super is an important part of your overall compensation. For more details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Putting It All Together: The Police Salary Victoria Context

If you are evaluating a **police salary Victoria**, remember that the figures above are averages, not specific to policing. The Victoria Police enterprise agreement sets pay rates based on rank, years of service, and qualifications. For example, a constable’s base rate may differ from the state average. Always refer to the official agreement or consult the Fair Work Ombudsman.

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool can help you compare offers. If you have a salary offer, divide by 52 and then by your weekly hours to find the implied hourly rate. For a **police salary Victoria**, the weekly hours are typically 38, but shift penalties and allowances may apply.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
